thread:
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident PDINC-73412 fired: service=inference-canary, symptom=OOM on quant nodes, urgency=high
incident-bot: Automated alert: canary deployment 2026-03-15T21:18Z failing healthchecks in eu-west-1, 5xx spike detected.
Devon K: seeing OOMs on a subset of canary pods. p95 token latency also spiking. Repro on canary only, not stable.
Samir: acked PDINC-73412 :white_check_mark: taking lead until handoff. Can we get the canary traffic down to 0%?
ops-bot: Runbook step: divert traffic -> run `redwoodctl traffic set inference-service --subset stable --pct 100`
Cara L: Samir on it? If we can divert, we should also toggle the new flag `enable_kv_prefetch` off. That flag landed in the canary image.
Samir: executing now.
Samir: ```
# divert traffic to stable
redwoodctl traffic set inference-service --subset stable --pct 100
# toggle feature flag
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $CFG_TOKEN" \
  https://config.redwood.internal/api/flags/enable_kv_prefetch \
  -d '{"value":false}'
```
Devon K: logs from one failing pod: ```
[2026-03-15T21:17:50Z] runtime: allocation failed: region exhausted
[2026-03-15T21:17:50Z] kernel: oom_killer invoked for process quant_runner
[2026-03-15T21:17:50Z] inference: allocation request 1.6G > available 1.2G
```
Maria G: metrics: canary cluster eu-west-1: 5xx rate jumped from 0.02% -> 0.9% in 5m, p95 token latency from 80ms -> 1.2s, error volume ~120 req/min. Customer visible errors on a small subset of requests (embedding endpoints).
Devon K: looks like memory blowup in quant path when the new prefetch is enabled and long contexts hit. Could be kv cache pre-allocation bug.
ops-bot: Canary traffic diverted successfully. Stable is at 100% for inference-service.
pagerduty-bot: PDINC-73412 acknowledged by Samir. Escalation paused.
Samir: I'm initiating canary rollback to previous image (v1.4.2). Will patch deployment and monitor.
Samir: ```
kubectl -n prod set image deploy/inference-svc inference=redwood/inference:v1.4.2-canary-rollback
kubectl rollout status deploy/inference-svc -n prod
```
Devon K: patch applied, pods terminating. Starting warmup on stable pool. Watching mem usage on quant nodes.
Maria G: telemetry update: errors trending down already, 5xx back to 0.03% in 3m. p95 returning to 90ms. Good.
Cara L: Thanks team. Samir can you stay with this and do the initial RCA notes, then hand off to Jun for overnight follow-up? Jun is on-call from 02:00 UTC.
Samir: Yep. I'll capture mitigation steps and config changes in the incident ticket. Also saving pod logs and heap snapshots to /s3/incidents/PDINC-73412/.
Devon K: quick note: quant nodes that ran OOM had kernel messages showing allocation pattern when sequence_length > 2048. Adding that to RCA.
Jun: Thanks — I'll take handoff if you need to leave. Please @mention me in the ticket with action items.
Samir: @Jun done. Main action items: (1) postmortem - root cause suspected kv prefetch allocation in quant path; (2) revert flag in canary rollout until we have memory-bounded prefetch; (3) add unit test for long-context mem usage; (4) validate autoscaler memory limits on quant nodes.
Cara L: Good. Also notify CS for any customers who saw degradation (small %, low latency hits) — Maria, can you draft a customer note?
Maria G: Drafting now. Will send to #customer-success for review. TL;DR: brief degradation in eu-west-1 during canary rollout; no broad data loss; rollback applied; stable behavior restored.
ops-bot: Incident mitigation checklist: traffic diverted, flag toggled, canary rolled back, monitoring restored. Awaiting confirmation to close.
Devon K: Confirming quant pod memory stable on last 10m sample. No new OOM events.
Samir: Closing PDINC-73412 in PagerDuty. Marking incident status: mitigated.
pagerduty-bot: PDINC-73412 status changed: Resolved by Samir at 2026-03-15T21:46Z.
incident-bot: Incident closed. Please file a postmortem in the incidents tracker and tag SRE + ML infra.
Cara L: Thanks everyone. We'll run a small postmortem tomorrow and prioritise the fix. :thumbsup:
Jun: I'll take the follow-up and link PRs to the ticket. Good handoff.
Samir: leaving notes in the ticket and adding heapdumps + perf traces. Signing off. :wave:
Maria G: Customer note posted to #customer-success, will follow up if any replies.
Devon K: filing a short runbook update to include the flag toggle path and the traffic diversion commands.
incident-bot: Thread archived.
